A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 22-page study, including readable equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Textual and visual comparisons establish that no material gaps limit assessment.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–3 report original experiments on PNS optimization, in-context learning, and supervised fine-tuning. Appendices E and G contain additional empirical evidence.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Section 5 and Tables 1–3, together with the case study and additional PNS results in Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, PS/PN estimation, the three intervention rollout strategies, and the use of optimized traces for in-context learning and fine-tuning are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain GSM-8k, MATH-500, AIME, and CommonsenseQA evaluation coverage. The fine-tuning sources, including MATH, MMLU, ZebraLogicBench, CommonsenseQA, and pre-2024 AIME, also match.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same unoptimized-trace comparisons, Standard/Fast-Solve/Reduction/CoD ICL baselines, and Original/Noncausal SFT comparators within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Models, metrics, prompts, the 1,229-trace fine-tuning dataset, training budgets, and inference settings remain unchanged. The renumbered inference footnotes retain the same 16,384-token limit.

E4.justification: The rollout-strategy comparisons, PNS analyses in Figure 3 and Appendix G, and MATH-500 ICL case study in Appendix E are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The Monte Carlo PNS estimator and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings match throughout Tables 1–3, Figure 3, and Appendices E and G. The changed superscripts on pages 7 and 9 are footnote numbers, not result revisions.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–5, Lemmas 1–3, Theorem 1, and the assumptions and proofs in Appendix A remain unchanged. Equation 1 only shifts with surrounding text.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating PNS into CoT, constructing efficient reasoning traces, and improving efficiency and accuracy through ICL and SFT.

C2.justification: The causal interpretations and limitations remain identical, including prompt sensitivity, difficult tasks, pruning-threshold selection, PNS estimation costs, and counterfactual-generation quality.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D and H retain identical prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime, and software information. Code and data access information is unchanged; the removed first-page footnote concerns author correspondence.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2, and Appendix F retain the same research positioning. Related-work lines moving between pages 2 and 3 are unchanged text.

P1.justification: v2 removes the corresponding-author markers for Xiao Xue and Jun Wang and their email footnote, updates the arXiv stamp, and renumbers subsequent footnotes. Body wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the correspondence footnote causes limited spacing and page-break changes across pages 1–3. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes administrative and minor layout edits while retaining the same scientific argument, results, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility documentation throughout the appendices. These changes establish no meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
